title: Pavlova
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Classic Australian pavlova with a crisp meringue shell, marshmallow centre, cream and fresh fruit.
instructions: Heat the oven to 120°C and line a tray with baking paper, drawing a 20 cm circle as a guide.
Whip egg whites to soft peaks, then add sugar one spoonful at a time until the meringue is glossy and firm.
Fold through cornflour, vinegar and vanilla gently, keeping as much air in the meringue as possible.
Spoon the meringue into the circle, shape high sides and a shallow centre, then bake until crisp outside.
Turn the oven off and cool the pavlova inside with the door slightly ajar to reduce cracking.
Top the completely cool shell with softly whipped cream and fruit immediately before serving.
tips: Keep all egg-yolk traces out of the whites.
commonMistakes: Opening the hot oven too soon can collapse the shell.
storage: Store the undecorated shell airtight for one day.

title: Lamingtons
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Soft Australian sponge squares coated in chocolate icing and coconut.
instructions: Cut a completely cooled butter cake into even squares and chill briefly so the sponge stays intact.
Whisk icing sugar, cocoa, milk and melted butter into a smooth, pourable chocolate coating.
Place coconut in a shallow tray and keep a rack nearby for the finished lamingtons.
Dip one cake square quickly in chocolate, coating all sides without soaking it until it falls apart.
Roll the coated square through coconut, using forks to keep fingers clean and the coating even.
Set on the rack until the chocolate layer is dry, then serve or store in an airtight container.
tips: Day-old cake is easiest to coat.
commonMistakes: Dipping warm cake makes crumbs shed.
substitutions: Split squares and add jam and cream.

title: Anzac Biscuits
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Golden chewy Australian ANZAC biscuits with oats, coconut and a buttery caramel flavour.
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C and line two trays with baking paper, allowing room for the biscuits to spread.
Combine oats, flour, coconut and brown sugar in a large bowl, breaking apart any sugar lumps.
Melt butter and golden syrup together over low heat until smooth but not bubbling hard.
Stir bicarbonate of soda into boiling water, then add it to the butter mixture; it will foam briefly.
Mix wet ingredients into dry ingredients, roll tablespoons of dough into balls and flatten them gently.
Bake until deep golden at the edges, then cool on the tray for softness or longer for a crisp finish.
tips: Use rolled oats, not instant oats.
substitutions: Use maple syrup when golden syrup is unavailable.
storage: Keep airtight up to one week.

title: Fairy Bread
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: A cheerful Australian party snack of buttered white bread covered in colourful sprinkles.
instructions: Set out fresh soft white bread and use a small offset spatula to spread every slice evenly with butter.
Pour hundreds and thousands into a shallow plate wide enough to fit a bread slice.
Press the buttered side of one slice firmly into the sprinkles so the whole surface is covered.
Lift the bread carefully, shake away loose sprinkles, and repeat with the remaining slices.
Trim crusts only if desired, keeping the slices intact until all sprinkle coating is complete.
Cut each slice into neat triangles and serve straight away for the freshest texture and colour.
tips: Use room-temperature butter so the bread does not tear.
commonMistakes: Using stale bread makes the triangles dry.

title: Tim Tam Cheesecake
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: No-bake chocolate Tim Tam cheesecake with a cookie crumb base and creamy filling.
instructions: Crush Tim Tams finely, combine with melted butter and press firmly into a lined springform pan.
Chill the base while you beat room-temperature cream cheese, icing sugar and vanilla until completely smooth.
Whip the cream to soft peaks in a separate bowl so it stays light when folded into the filling.
Fold cream through the cream-cheese mixture, then stir through chopped Tim Tam pieces gently.
Spread the filling over the chilled base, smooth the top and refrigerate until firm throughout.
Decorate with extra Tim Tams immediately before slicing with a warm knife for clean portions.
tips: Let cream cheese soften before beating.
commonMistakes: Folding in over-whipped cream can make the filling grainy.
substitutions: Use chocolate sandwich cookies if Tim Tams are unavailable.

title: Caramel Slice
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Australian caramel slice with a shortbread base, baked caramel middle and chocolate top.
instructions: Line a square tin and combine flour, coconut, brown sugar and melted butter for the crumbly base.
Press the mixture into the tin evenly and bake until lightly golden before adding the caramel layer.
Warm condensed milk, butter and golden syrup over low heat, stirring constantly until thick and glossy.
Pour caramel over the base and bake gently until the surface is set with a slight wobble.
Cool fully, then melt chocolate and spread it in a smooth, even layer across the caramel.
Chill until set, then cut with a warm knife into tidy squares before serving.
tips: Cut before the chocolate becomes rock hard.
commonMistakes: High heat can scorch the caramel.
substitutions: Use dark chocolate for a less sweet top.

title: Neenish Tarts
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Classic Australian Neenish tarts with jam, cream filling and signature two-tone icing.
instructions: Roll sweet pastry thinly, line tart tins and chill the shells so they hold their shape in the oven.
Blind-bake until crisp and golden, then cool completely before adding any filling or icing.
Spoon a small layer of raspberry jam into each shell to create the traditional fruity base.
Whip cream to firm peaks and pipe or spoon it over the jam without overfilling the pastry.
Make white icing, divide it, then tint one half pink and stir cocoa into the other half.
Ice half of each tart with pink and half with chocolate icing, meeting cleanly down the centre.
tips: Cool pastry shells completely before filling.
commonMistakes: Runny icing will spill over the tarts.
substitutions: Use lemon curd instead of jam.
storage: Refrigerate filled tarts up to two days.

title: Lamington Cake
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: A celebration-size lamington cake layered with chocolate, coconut, jam and cream.
instructions: Level cooled sponge layers so the finished cake sits flat and is easy to slice cleanly.
Spread one layer with raspberry jam and softly whipped cream, leaving a small border around the edge.
Place the second sponge layer on top and chill briefly so the filling becomes stable.
Whisk cocoa, icing sugar and milk into a spreadable chocolate icing with no dry lumps.
Cover the top and sides of the cake with icing, then press coconut over every exposed surface.
Chill until set, then slice with a warm knife and serve with extra berries if desired.
tips: Use chilled cake layers for neater icing.
commonMistakes: Warm sponge can melt the cream filling.
substitutions: Use strawberry jam instead of raspberry.

title: Hot Cross Buns
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Soft spiced hot cross buns studded with fruit, finished with flour crosses and glossy glaze.
instructions: Combine flour, yeast, sugar and spice, then add warm milk, melted butter and egg to make a soft dough.
Knead until smooth and elastic, then fold through sultanas and leave covered until doubled in size.
Divide the risen dough into equal balls, arrange closely in a lined pan and let them rise again.
Pipe flour-and-water paste in crosses over each bun just before baking.
Bake until deeply golden and the buns sound hollow when tapped on their bases.
Warm apricot jam with a little water and brush it over hot buns for a glossy finish.
tips: Use warm, not hot, milk for the yeast.
commonMistakes: Adding fruit before the dough develops can tear it.
substitutions: Use chopped dried apricots with raisins.
storage: Freeze cooled buns up to one month.

title: Australian Damper
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Simple rustic Australian damper bread with a crisp crust and soft centre.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C and line a baking tray, keeping ingredients cool for a tender crumb.
Rub cold butter into self-raising flour and salt until the mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs.
Pour in milk gradually and bring the dough together with a knife without overworking it.
Turn onto a floured surface, pat into a round loaf and score a deep cross across the top.
Bake until golden and hollow-sounding when tapped underneath, covering loosely if it browns too fast.
Rest for ten minutes, slice while warm and serve with butter, jam or soup.
tips: Handle the dough as little as possible.
substitutions: Use water instead of milk for a traditional camp-style loaf.
storage: Best on baking day; toast leftovers.

title: Chicken Tray Bake
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Moroccan-style Australian chicken tray bake with roasted vegetables, chickpeas and warming spices.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C and toss chicken thighs with olive oil, paprika, cumin, salt and pepper.
Spread onion, carrots and drained chickpeas across a large roasting tray in an even layer.
Nestle seasoned chicken among the vegetables, skin-side up, so the skin can brown and crisp.
Roast until chicken is cooked through and vegetables are tender, turning vegetables once if needed.
Squeeze lemon over the hot tray and let it stand for five minutes so the juices settle.
Scatter coriander over the chicken and serve directly from the tray with couscous or salad.
tips: Use a large tray so ingredients roast rather than steam.
substitutions: Use sweet potato instead of carrots.

title: Slow Cooker Lamb Chops
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Tender slow-cooker lamb chops with potatoes, carrots and simple savoury pan juices.
instructions: Season the lamb chops on both sides with garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, salt and black pepper.
Spread sliced onion, cubed potatoes and sliced carrots across the base of the slow cooker.
Set the seasoned lamb chops over the vegetables in a single layer where possible for even cooking.
Pour beef stock around the vegetables, keeping the seasoned surface of the chops mostly uncovered.
Cook on low until the lamb chops are tender and the potatoes and carrots are easily pierced with a fork.
Rest the chops briefly, spoon the savoury cooking juices over them and serve with the vegetables.
tips: Arrange the chops in one layer when your slow cooker size allows.
commonMistakes: Adding too much liquid can dilute the savoury cooking juices.
substitutions: Use sweet potato in place of regular potato.
storage: Refrigerate leftovers for up to three days and reheat until hot.

title: Australian Beef Burger
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Australian burger with the lot: juicy beef, beetroot, egg, pineapple, cheese and fresh salad.
instructions: Shape seasoned beef mince into four loose patties, making a small indentation in each centre.
Cook patties on a hot grill or skillet until browned, adding cheese for the final minute to melt.
Grill pineapple rings and cook eggs until the whites are set while keeping yolks to your preference.
Toast buns lightly so they can hold juicy fillings without becoming soggy.
Layer tomato sauce, lettuce, tomato, beef, beetroot, pineapple and egg on the bun bases.
Add onion, close the burgers carefully and serve immediately with napkins and hot chips.
tips: Avoid pressing patties while they cook.
commonMistakes: Overloading a small bun makes it impossible to eat.
substitutions: Use grilled onion instead of raw onion.
storage: Cooked patties refrigerate up to two days; assemble fresh.
